Definition: Mikajah, the name of three Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Micaiah son of Imlah is the prophet Ahab hates because he never tells the king what he wants to hear. Summoned to bless a war, he first repeats the court prophets' lie and then speaks the truth plainly: Israel scattered on the hills, without a shepherd. Ahab has him fed on bread and water until he returns in peace — and Micaiah answers that if Ahab returns in peace, the LORD has not spoken by him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Micaiah is the test of a true prophet: he would rather sit in prison on God's word than stand in the palace on the king's.
